title: What If the World Ran Out of Copper?

scenes.text: What if the world ran out of copper? Almost everything with a wire would stall.
Miners dig up about 23 million tons of copper every year.
An electric car uses around 60 kilograms of it, more than twice a gasoline car.
Wind and solar power need 4 to 12 times more copper than fossil fuel plants.
Known reserves are about 980 million tons, roughly four decades at today's pace.
But scientists estimate billions of tons more remain undiscovered, and recycling already supplies about 30 percent.

description:
What if the world ran out of copper?
We mine about 23 million tons a year, and clean energy needs far more of it.
What should we run through next?
